event.summary: Failed container rebuild discards the previous usable images
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: rebuilding a working container recipe can delete its usable software and installation images even when the replacement fails. Future launches must rebuild and can remain blocked by the same installer, network or edited-base failure. Details: prepare_images removes both state.image and state.prepared into retired_images before calling prepare_images_owned. On any failure its cleanup calls retire_images, which deletes these prior images when no containers use them. This contradicts SPEC.md, Container sessions: 'Superseded Farhelm-built images are removed after successful replacement once no container uses them.' SPEC_impl.md, Podman places, creation and images likewise says 'After successful build/preparation replacement, remove a superseded owned image once no container uses it.' The current source records are already gone if cleanup fails or the helm exits. Keep old current records until a replacement software image is durably published, while forcing software() to build for an admitted Rebuild independently of cache presence. Suggested bucket: high/material UX. Confidence: confirmed by source and explicit contract; caller route still being inspected for completeness. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: no established loss-of-user-work route; retire_images uses non-forcing removal and checks any container's use, so existing containers are protected. This finding concerns recipe availability and unnecessary rebuilding. No execution or reproduction performed.

event.summary: Interrupted image capture can permanently block recipe cleanup
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: stopping the helm at the wrong point in an image build can leave a recipe permanently undeletable, even when its recorded image never existed. Its container host also remains protected from removal or retargeting by the retained recipe artifact. Details: Podman::commit persists a fresh lookup tag in retired_images before issuing podman commit (podman.rs:505-524). A helm crash after that durable write but before command dispatch leaves an absent tag that can never appear; a transport failure before remote dispatch has the same effect. On every retry, retire_images_unlocked rejects absence unless image_id(&id).is_ok() (build.rs:748-752); a lookup tag cannot satisfy that predicate. The only recovery branch converts a tag after positive image inspection (706-718), so it cannot settle this crash window. git grep over all retired_images writers found no alternate tag settlement path: commit clears on its own synchronous refusal/success; publication removes only exact canonical IDs; cleanup removes a tag only after positive observation. clean_images always calls this function before removing the place state (779-788), and delete_recipe_owned returns on provider cleanup error before deleting the recipe row (tensorlake/recipes.rs:610-614). SPEC_impl.md:6521 requires failures to retain records, and :6570 promises retryable explicit cleanup; conservative immediate retention is correct but permanent absence needs a bounded or otherwise certified settlement mechanism, such as a durable remotely owned commit job/outcome. Do not fix by immediately treating an absent tag as proof of failed commit: a disconnected commit may still publish. The existing tests.rs:464 scenario only covers absence followed by eventual image appearance, not the no-send crash window. Suggested bucket: high/material UX. Confidence: confirmed by source crash-window and exhaustive state-writer analysis; no execution or reproduction. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: no established security or user-work-loss consequence; the established impact is permanently blocked cleanup and host administration. Rarity does not change that impact.

event.summary: Interrupted image capture can permanently block recipe cleanup
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b; settlement paths checked through pinned tip 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db. TLDR: a helm crash during an image build can leave the recipe permanently undeletable even though the recorded image never existed, and block removal or retargeting of its container host. The decisive no-dispatch window is after Podman::commit's awaited durable retired_images.push(tag) completes (podman.rs:505-511) and before the following command future is polled/dispatched (:512-525); stopping the helm there destroys the stack frame, so its later refusal/success settlement cannot run and no image can later appear from that invocation. Enumerated every production retirement-tag settlement at the pinned tip: (1) commit's own definite refusal plus absent tag clears it (:526-534); (2) successful commit parses an image ID then replaces the tag (:542-550); (3) retire_images_unlocked sees an existing tagged image, verifies ownership, persists its canonical ID, checks all containers and removes without force (build.rs:690-747); (4) absent canonical IDs can be cleared (:748-757). None settles an absent lookup tag after the no-dispatch crash. Software/prepared publication removes canonical IDs, not earlier random tags (:219,:387). The sole place-map removal is clean_images :788, reached only after tag cleanup succeeds (:785-787). Full searches for retired_images, state.podman, whole-state reset and recipe state SQL found no other production reset: definition saves and historical migrations change spec_json only; recipe deletion refuses needs_cleanup (tensorlake/recipes.rs:414-420). Leftover deletion removes containers, not recipe image records (podman.rs:725-763). Host removal/retarget checks retained PodmanRecipeState::needs_cleanup in store/podman.rs:213-249. git log/diff across the remainder of the range shows no later change to these paths; the only podman.rs follow-up changes an unrelated lifecycle lock. SPEC_impl.md:6521 requires failed cleanup records retained and :6570 requires retryable explicit cleanup; retaining ambiguity immediately is necessary, but this crash window has no recovery through the product. Keep original high/material UX bucket and blocked-cleanup/host-administration consequence. Confidence: confirmed source crash-window and enumerated production settlement analysis; no execution or reproduction. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: no established security/user-work-loss route. Fix caveat: absence alone is NOT proof a remotely dispatched commit has stopped. Do not clear tags immediately or apply a guessed age bound without establishing remote process completion. A durable remotely owned operation/outcome or another certified completion mechanism is needed; the finding does not authorize unsafe deletion. Existing tests cover absence followed by positive image appearance, not this never-dispatched case. No priority lowering.

event.summary: Container job completion lacks a final fleet invalidation
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: a recipe list reader can retain Preparing and a disabled Rebuild button after container image work has completed, until another change refreshes the list or it is reopened. Details: place_view derives building from podman_jobs membership (build.rs:601-610). start_podman publishes the job result at 723, then PodmanJobAdmission::drop removes the registry entry at 443-446, without publishing a fleet invalidation afterward. prepare_images sends its final event at podman/build.rs:288 while this admission guard still exists; its success path also publishes Ready at :404 while the job is still registered. A concurrent GET served between that event and admission removal truthfully reads building=true but spends the last invalidation on that state. The Rebuild endpoint returns 202 without a later completion invalidation (hosts.rs:4402-4407); FleetEvents explicitly carries no payload and asks readers to reread current state (feed.rs:14-30). Unlike the existing Tensorlake task at the earlier reviewed revision 56040bb964270bb40d191902173dbb84b3ba78fc, build.rs:642-653, Podman does not bump after registry removal. The new per-place GUI caller is integrated in the next commit 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462: RecipeList restarts place_status on fleet notices or changed host-probe observations (tensorlake/recipes.rs:367-385), and RecipePlaces disables Rebuild on row.building (containers_settings.rs:257-260). A settled, unchanged probe does not provide a build-completion event. At the reviewed 5665983 revision this is a backend feed-contract defect; that subsequent caller establishes the visible consequence after integration. Fix completion publication to remove admission before bumping, also handling panics/cancellation consistently. Suggested bucket: other, a source-proven notification ordering race whose occurrence and duration were not measured. Confidence: confirmed missing invalidation and source-supported concurrent schedule, not execution-observed behavior. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: no established security or user-work loss route. Caveat on the original early-prerequisite concern: a failed fresh probe may become visible through the GUI's place-observation refresh, so silent prerequisite failure is not claimed as a separate confirmed consequence.

event.summary: Custom-image login lookup unnecessarily requires /root
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. Discovery pass 1. TLDR: a valid custom container base without a /root directory cannot build, even when the selected login account has a usable home and meets all documented requirements. Farhelm fails before it can resolve that account. Source: software selects a custom reference/user without managed bootstrap (build.rs:142-150) and immediately calls login (:151). login runs getent through self.script using root_user (:65-73), whose home is hard-coded /root (:411-417). RemoteRoute::container_argv turns that guessed home into podman exec --user 0 --workdir /root as well as HOME (access.rs:193-230). No prior custom-base step creates /root: pull_base only pulls/inspects and helper starts /sbin/init; the readiness check for the actual login occurs only after lookup (:152-159). SPEC.md:471-475 requires systemd, passwordless sudo, Ubuntu/Debian apt, bash, curl and git; neither it nor SPEC_impl.md:6552-6559 requires root to have /root. A base can satisfy those requirements with its selected user's home elsewhere and no /root. The selected login is precisely what getent is meant to discover, so guessing another account's directory is an unrelated prerequisite. External primary checks, not execution here: official Podman exec docs define --workdir as the execution working directory (https://docs.podman.io/en/stable/markdown/podman-exec.1.html); v4.9.3 source passes WorkDir into opts.Cwd (https://github.com/containers/podman/blob/v4.9.3/libpod/container_exec.go#L1012-L1025) and into the OCI process cwd without creating it (https://github.com/containers/podman/blob/v4.9.3/libpod/oci_conmon_exec_common.go#L648-L650). The upstream crun missing-workdir report confirms exec fails at chdir, rather than creating the directory (https://github.com/containers/crun/issues/1823). Fix by using a guaranteed neutral working directory such as / for the privileged account-observation step, then use the observed selected account home for its actual setup. Do not impose /root as a new undocumented custom-base requirement. Suggested bucket: other/custom-base compatibility; no measured prevalence or material-user-impact threshold claimed. Confidence: confirmed source and upstream exec semantics; no local tests, reproduction or runtime observation. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none in supplied neighbour records; no prohibited sources searched. Could-be-highest: no security or user-work-loss route; this blocks a new build, with ordinary failed-helper cleanup. Caveats: managed Ubuntu normally has /root; custom images retaining it are unaffected. Existing built images can postpone this until preparation/account lookup is required. The lead's original custom-base build-failure consequence is retained.

event.summary: Owned-image cleanup can prune an untagged user-owned base
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b; this assigned build implementation is unchanged through pinned tip 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db. Discovery pass 2. TLDR: cleaning up a recipe can also delete its user-owned local base image when that image has no tag. If that local image is the user's only retained copy of its contents, recipe deletion destroys work outside the helm-owned artifacts the cleanup is supposed to remove. Details: retire_images_unlocked checks the explicit target's ownership labels, then invokes podman image rm -- <id> without --no-prune (build.rs:690-743). Podman's default removal also recursively prunes dangling parent images; those implicit targets never pass Farhelm's ownership-label check. Shipped input route: RecipeBase::ContainerImage accepts any nonempty NUL-free reference (farhelm-proto/src/recipes.rs:788-797), including a local image ID. pull_base accepts an already-existing image by that reference, skips pulling or tagging it, and rejects only a prepared Farhelm checkpoint (build.rs:808-837). Thus a user may select an untagged local custom base with their chosen login account, required systemd/tools and otherwise valid contents. software runs a helper from that reference (:142-150) and commits a new owned layer (:203-224); preparation makes another owned child. With no containers left using these artifacts, clean_images appends software and prepared for removal (:781-785). Removing an owned layer can make its untagged user-owned parent dangling and prune its image record/content automatically. The saved recipe reference is not a Podman tag or container reference, so it does not protect the parent. No UI control or cleanup path adds a protective tag to the existing base. The contract is explicit: SPEC.md:4811 says 'User-owned base images are retained'; SPEC_impl.md:6566-6568 says 'Never delete a user's base image.' Fix by passing --no-prune to owned-image removal and continuing to remove only separately recorded, verified owned IDs; nonforcing removal alone does not constrain implicit parent pruning. Primary source checks at the supported Podman floor: v4.9.3 rmi docs describe default dangling-parent deletion and the --no-prune option (https://docs.podman.io/en/v4.9.3/markdown/podman-rmi.1.html). Vendored libimage/image.go:496-518 returns early only for NoPrune, otherwise checks Parent.IsDangling then recursively removes it without a Farhelm ownership predicate; :185-193 defines dangling as no names and no children (https://github.com/containers/podman/blob/v4.9.3/vendor/github.com/containers/common/libimage/image.go#L496-L518). Podman ABI passes opts.NoPrune through (pkg/domain/infra/abi/images.go:558-568). Podman commit imports the source builder and commits without squash/history omission (libpod/container_commit.go:57-70,160); vendored Buildah image.go:256-278 preserves base history and :631-660 appends the new layer history. Libimage layer_tree.go:147-152,263-340 recognizes the corresponding parent via layer/history. These establish the ordinary committed-image ancestry and prune route, rather than inferring data deletion from shared layers alone. Suggested bucket: highest/security or loss of user-owned work for a sole-copy local base; the direct unwanted-base deletion is established independently of whether a particular image contains irreplaceable data. Could-be-highest: yes, a valid shipped image-ID input can name a sole-copy user-authored image, and deletion removes that original outside the owned-artifact boundary. Confidence: confirmed source/contract route, conditional on an untagged local base and no other container/image reference that keeps it non-dangling; not observed execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none in supplied neighbour records. Caveats: tagged/digest-named bases remain protected by their names; other dependent images/containers may prevent pruning. No claim of deleting a currently used base forcibly, no claim that all recipes are affected, and no claim of measured frequency. Original l8 unwanted-base-removal consequence is preserved and its possible work-loss route is now explicit. No tests, builds, reproductions or live-install actions performed.
